reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E4) directly supports the catalytic activity, a-C tribolayer formation from ethanol, and friction reduction for spray-coated 2D HEA nanoflakes at room temperature. However, no cited passage provides evidence for the claimed wide service-temperature range (e.g., up to 600°C), leaving that key premise unsupported.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes are catalytically active and can dissociate organic molecules during sliding
The catalytic dissociation of organics (e.g., ethanol) leads to in situ formation of an amorphous carbon tribolayer
The a-C tribolayer reduces friction and wear by lowering shear and preventing metal-metal contact
A simple spray coating of 2D HEA nanoflakes can be applied to a surface to provide this lubrication
The mechanism is effective across a wide temperature range from room temperature up to moderately high temperatures
